ledger.claim: The arrival test in POL-NS-01(b) fails on the driver's own trace. Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence at or before the recorded 'arrived' event; for this TRANSPORT_HUB pickup the geofence radius under POL-NS-02 is 150 m, and the first qualifying in-radius fix is at 07:44:14 — 369 seconds after the 07:38:05 arrival event — with no qualifying in-radius fix at or before it. One broken limb is enough, and the penalty for a broken limb is that the fee is not chargeable.

The dwell requirement in POL-NS-01(c) also fails. For TRANSPORT_HUB the minimum continuous in-geofence dwell is 300 seconds, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap. The longest qualifying run is 236 seconds (07:44:14 to 07:48:10, 25 fixes), a 64-second shortfall, and the driver terminated the trip at 07:48:10 while that clock was still short of the minimum.

With the effective in-geofence dwell at 236 seconds against a 300-second minimum, POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee non-chargeable and refunds it in full — whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages — and no driver compensation is payable. The $6.00 already returned on the ledger (refund_issued_sgd 6.00, payment_status REFUNDED) is therefore the correct disposition and should stand.

There is no accumulation route for the driver under POL-NS-06(i). The trace holds a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1, accumulated dwell 236 seconds, no excursions), and no traffic advisory covers this pickup road or the waiting period: EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight 0.0 under POL-GEN-02. Its absence is citable, but it can add nothing to the dwell, and under POL-NS-06(ii) a missing advisory never reduces the required minimum.

The 07:38:05 arrival tap cannot start the waiting clock. The trace's only in-radius presence is the closing 236 seconds, while the driver's mean distance from the pin across the whole trace is 888.89 m; recomputing the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, as POL-NS-05 directs, yields a corrected dwell of 236 seconds against the 300-second minimum, so the fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable under POL-NS-05(i).

Nothing in the record shows a rider who was elsewhere. All 88 rider fixes fall inside the 200 m TRANSPORT_HUB rider-presence radius set by POL-NS-04(c), sitting between 50.53 m and 91.70 m from the pickup pin from 07:43:10 onwards, which matches her account that she was at the PHV bay looking for the car. Her presence is not needed to win the fee point — POL-NS-06 refunds it either way — but the record does not support the driver's no-show narrative.

The driver's chat message of 07:38:40, 'im at the phv bay', is contradicted by his own telemetry: the trace shows no in-radius fix until 07:44:14, over five minutes later, so the account of a ten-minute wait at the bay is not made out on the proximity test in POL-NS-02.

The finding rests on clean data, so this dispute can be decided rather than hedged or held: the trace has 108 fixes with no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0), the arrived event falls within 5 seconds of a GPS fix so no clock-skew limb is engaged, and the $6.00 charged reconciles with the fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee of 6.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00. No limb of POL-NS-08 applies to the facts that decide this case.

No escalation trigger exists. The rider profile records no_show_disputes_30d of 0, and both profiles record disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged and there is no basis for withholding the outcome pending a human reviewer — a held fee is not a refunded fee.

The relief the driver seeks is restoration of a charge the platform has already reversed. On this driver-filed dispute the ledger stands at refund_issued_sgd 6.00 with payment_status REFUNDED, and under POL-GEN-03 a disposition of NO_ACTION leaves the rider refunded — it never means 'restore the charge'.

The arrival test is satisfied on the code-computed facts. The driver's trace contains 25 qualifying position fixes inside the 150 m arrival radius that applies to a TRANSPORT_HUB pickup, held in a single continuous in-geofence run from 07:44:14 to 07:48:10, so the driver did reach the pickup point at Tampines Bus Interchange PHV bay (pickup venue_id VEN-TAMPINES-INTERCHANGE). The rider's account of a car that could not be found is therefore a perception difference about the bay, not a driver who never turned up, and the case turns on dwell, not on arrival.

Two of the four limbs of the baseline charge are squarely satisfied. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 07:38:05 (limb (a)), the trip was terminated by the driver at 07:48:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises — and the record shows no boarding event (limb (d)). The only limb in contest is the dwell measure.

The amount charged is not inflated and raises no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d). Applying the fee_schedule resolution rule — the GREATER of the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee — the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee is SGD 6.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00, and the higher figure is exactly the SGD 6.00 cancellation-fee line in the fare breakdown, with the zone class and vehicle tier both read from the trip record. There is nothing here for the rider to attack as a mis-tariff.

The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 does not open. Limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message FROM THE RIDER during the waiting window; the chat log holds three messages — the system arrival notice at 07:38:06 and two driver messages — and nothing at all from the rider, and the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, so the 120-second reply test in limb (b) is never even reached. The rider's own track places her stationary (distinct_speeds_kph is [0.0]) between 50.5 m and 91.7 m of the pin across 88 fixes from 07:43:10, so she was at the bay: presence was not the problem, engagement was.

The waiting period the rider paid for was served, measured on the record's own clock. The trip record's waiting interval runs from the 07:38:05 arrived event to the 07:48:10 cancellation — wait_time_min 10.1, or 605 seconds — against a 300-second minimum for TRANSPORT_HUB. The driver accepts the GPS-derived in-geofence run of 236 seconds (shortfall_sec 64) and does not dispute that computation, but POL-NS-05, the only clause that displaces the arrival marker and recomputes the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, is not engaged on this record: its triggers require the trace to place the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or moving at 15 km/h or more, at the arrival timestamp, and the code-computed set carries no distance or speed reading at 07:38:05, only whole-trace aggregates (min 30.3 m, mean 888.9 m, max 2,749.6 m). Absent a false-marker finding the arrival marker and the recorded waiting interval stand, POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met, and the driver is owed 80 per cent of the SGD 6.00 fee, SGD 4.80, under POL-NS-07.

No profile counter withholds or blocks that payout. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a termination rate above 0.08. The driver profile records 3 no-show terminations against 88 completed trips in 30 days, a rate of 0.034, so the check does not trip and compensation is payable rather than withheld. On the other side, both profiles record disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so the repeat-dispute and abuse triggers in POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged either.

If the Judge displaces the arrival marker — the alternative case the rider must make — the dispute falls under POL-NS-03 rather than POL-NS-06, and the driver is still owed a payment. The recorded pickup is a hub with registered_pickup_points of 2, and neither party named a sub-location anywhere in the chat: the driver's two messages say only 'im at the phv bay' and 'boss? cannot wait very long here, this bay cannot park', and the rider's statement says only 'the PHV bay'. On the derived facts the record does not place the driver inside the arrival radius until 07:44:14, 369 seconds after his arrival marker. Where the mislocation is attributable to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, POL-NS-03(ii) directs a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 per cent of the cancellation fee — SGD 3.00 — to the driver, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider, and the code-computed money block publishes SGD 3.00 for this charge on that clause.

If the Judge instead takes the 236-second in-geofence run as the operative dwell, the matter should go to a human reviewer rather than be closed against the driver. On that reading two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on arrival: the trip record puts the driver 'arrived' at 07:38:05 and records a 10.1-minute wait, while the trace shows no qualifying in-radius fix before 07:44:14, and the only clause that would resolve the conflict — POL-NS-05 — cannot be run because the derived set carries no distance or speed reading at the arrival marker. The advisory that would answer the kerb question the driver's own 07:44:20 message raises ('this bay cannot park') is also absent: EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING, has no payload and can carry no fact, so limp (i) of POL-NS-06 cannot be run. That unresolved conflict is what the escalation route is for, and the disputed fee should be held rather than closed out.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The $6.00 no-show cancellation fee is NOT chargeable, so the state of the ledger stays exactly as it is — refund_issued_sgd 6.00, payment_status REFUNDED — and the driver's request to restore the charge is denied. Under POL-GEN-03 that disposition is NO_ACTION, which is party-relative: on a driver-filed dispute over a fee the platform has already reversed, it leaves the rider refunded. No money moves; no compensation is paid.

WHY. POL-NS-01 charges the fee only if all four conditions hold. Two are met: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 07:38:05 (limb (a)), and the trip was terminated by the driver at 07:48:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event (limb (d)). Two fail.

(1) Limb (c), dwell. The pickup is a TRANSPORT_HUB, so the minimum continuous in-geofence dwell is 300 seconds. POL-NS-01(c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. The first qualifying fix is at 07:44:14 and the run ends at the 07:48:10 cancellation — 236 seconds, a 64-second shortfall (shortfall_sec 64, one qualifying run, 25 qualifying fixes against a 150 m arrival radius for a hub). The trip record's wait_time_min of 10.1 (about 605 seconds) runs from the driver's own arrival tap, and a marker the driver set does not start the clock that limb (c) defines.

(2) Limb (b). There is no qualifying in-radius fix at or before the 07:38:05 arrival event; the first is 369 seconds later (dwell_start_offset_sec -369). The driver was not inside the pickup geofence when he tapped arrived, and his 07:38:40 message 'im at the phv bay' is contradicted by his own trace.

Once a limb of POL-NS-01 fails the fee is not chargeable at all, and POL-NS-06 makes the shortfall a full refund with no driver compensation payable, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied.

DRIVER ADVOCATE, ANSWERED. Your POL-NS-02 point is accepted so far as it goes: 25 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m hub radius exist, so the arrival test under POL-NS-02 is satisfied and the driver genuinely reached the bay — but that is precisely why the case turns on dwell, and the dwell is 236 s against 300 s. Your POL-NS-01(a)/(d) point is accepted; your POL-NS-01(b)/(c) reading is not, for the reasons above. Your amount point is accepted: $6.00 is the correct charge under the fee_schedule resolution rule, the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect — but a correctly computed amount does not make a non-chargeable fee chargeable. Your POL-NS-05 argument that the arrival marker stands is rejected: POL-NS-05 is not the only route to measuring the clock from GPS entry — POL-NS-01(c) does so itself — and in any event the recomputed dwell is the same 236 s, so POL-NS-05(i) would refund in full and POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral does NOT fire because qualifying in-geofence fixes do exist. Your POL-NS-03 alternative is rejected: POL-NS-03 requires the driver to be stationary for the required dwell OUTSIDE the arrival radius but within 400 m; the driver's stationary fixes sit inside the 150 m radius at 30–92 m from the pin, and the required dwell was not served in any event, so no platform-funded goodwill ($3.00) arises. Your POL-NS-07/anti-farming point is accepted on its own terms — no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below 4) and 3/88 = 0.034 (below 0.08), so the check does not trip — but compensation is not payable for a different reason: POL-NS-07 only pays where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Your POL-NS-09 escalation argument is rejected: the apparent conflict between a driver-set 'arrived' marker and the platform's trace is exactly what POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 are written to resolve (the marker is judged against the trace), and no limb of POL-NS-09 engages — confidence is well above the 0.70 floor, both profiles show disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d).

RIDER ADVOCATE, ANSWERED. Your limb (b) and limb (c) failures are accepted and decide the case. Your POL-NS-06 point is accepted: the fee is refunded in full and no compensation is payable, and the $6.00 already returned is the correct disposition. Your POL-NS-06(i) point is accepted: the trace holds a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1, no excursions) and EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no separate intervals can be summed and, under POL-NS-06(ii), a missing advisory never reduces the 300 s minimum. Your rider-presence point is accepted as a finding: all 88 rider fixes sit 50.5–91.7 m from the pin inside the 200 m hub radius, which is consistent with the rider's own account. Your POL-NS-08 clean-data point is accepted: the trace has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0), the arrival event falls within seconds of a GPS fix so no clock-skew limb is engaged, the chat log's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 3, and the $6.00 line reconciles with the fee schedule. Your no-escalation point and your POL-GEN-03 point are accepted. One correction to your framing: because the FILING party here is the driver, the emitted ruling value is NO_ACTION, not FULL_REFUND — the outcome for the rider is the same (the refund stands), but POL-GEN-03 names the outcome for the filer.

CONFIDENCE AND EVIDENCE. The deciding facts — the 236-second in-geofence dwell and the absence of any qualifying in-radius fix at or before the arrival marker — are carried by EV-GPS-00209 and EV-TRIP-00209, and no artifact relied on is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is not reduced. EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is absent (weight 0.0) and carries no fact; its absence only confirms that POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable. No profile field outside those POL-GEN-01 permits as a ground was used to decide anything. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 escalation floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
